newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: New swaps hike Old Mutual offshore fund investment.
newsitem.headline: New swaps hike Old Mutual offshore fund investment.

text.p: Old Mutual, South Africa's biggest investment group, said on Thursday it was concluding a new asset swap programme which will mean around 90 percent of its Global Equity Fund mutual fund is invested offshore.

"We believe that Global Equity Fund will be the first South African unit trust to be truly offshore after the concessions announced by Finance Minister Trevor Manuel in the budget (on March 12)," said Old Mutual Unit Trusts managing director Selwyn Feldman.
The budget gave institutions the go ahead to invest up to 10 percent of their total assets abroad and not, as before, 10 percent of each individual mutual fund, known locally as unit trusts.
The move could more than double mutual funds' investments offshore to 4.4 billion rand, equating to 10 percent of the industry's December 1996 asset base of 43.8 billion rand.
Feldman said Old Mutual Unit Trusts would make full use of the concessions, but he warned that the 10 percent ceiling would have to be raised.

"Initially legislators appeared to take the view that the ceiling would not need to be increased as unit trust management companies were unlikely to fully utilise this concession," Feldman, who also chairs the Association of Unit Trusts, told a presentation on unit trusts.
"This is now proving incorrect and the industry will be requesting the financial authorities to amend the regulations."
Old Mutual manages nearly 10 billion rand in mutual funds.
Its Global fund has assets of 553.5 million rand of which some 135 million rand, or 25 percent, were invested offshore by the end of March.
"Agreement has been reached in principle with asset swap parties to increase this to 80-90 percent with a short period," Feldman said.
Old Mutual Unit Trusts has approval to accumulate a total of 970 million rand in foreign assets, he added.

Old Mutual Investors' Funds, the country's largest mutual fund with assets of 5.5 billion rand, has also undertaken an asset swap programme and now has some 400 million rand or seven percent of assets offshore.
Feldman said Old Mutual's South African funds were likely to diversify up to 20 percent of their portfolio at the portfolio manager's discretion.
